name: Garryaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Garrya lindheimeri through evergreen leathery opposite leaves, dioecious petal-less aments, 4-sepal/4-stamen male flowers, reduced female flowers and dark berries; collapse the source subspecies name into the current species.

project_scope.selection_mode: Source Garrya ovata subsp. lindheimeri + Garrya lindheimeri collapsed to one current concept
project_scope.note: Current Kew/FNA accepts Garrya lindheimeri; native range is southwestern Texas to northeastern Mexico.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for opposite leathery leaves and axillary catkin-like aments on a woody evergreen shrub.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Shrubs or small trees; leaves opposite, simple, coriaceous and entire to slightly undulate.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Plants dioecious. Flowers are petal-less in axillary aments. Staminate flowers have 4 sepals and 4 stamens; pistillate flowers have only 2 small/rudimentary sepals and an inferior ovary with 2 styles.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Fleshy berry, dark blue to black when mature and becoming pale/grayish as it dries, usually with 1–2 seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite leathery leaves + separate male/female petal-less aments + dark berry = Garryaceae/Garrya.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: opposite leaf pair → male ament → female ament → flower anatomy → berry → lindheimeri leaf surface → subspecies synonym card
visual_lesson.intro: Silktassel is a wind-pollinated asterid that looks nothing like a typical showy-flowered one: its flowers are stripped down into separate male and female catkins.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the opposite leathery leaves
steps.look_for: Pairs of broad coriaceous leaves at the nodes; G. lindheimeri leaves are comparatively large with flat smooth margins.

steps.title: 2 · Separate male and female plants
steps.look_for: Male aments more flexible and pollen-oriented; female aments bearing sessile pistillate flowers and later fruits.
steps.why_it_matters: Dioecy is essential to reading the plant.

steps.title: 3 · Open a male flower
steps.look_for: Four narrow sepals, no petals, four stamens.

steps.title: 4 · Open a female flower
steps.look_for: Two small/rudimentary sepals, no petals, inferior ovary and two styles.

steps.title: 5 · Follow the female ament to berries
steps.look_for: Blue-black fleshy berries becoming paler gray-white when dry.

steps.title: 6 · Collapse the duplicate source concept
steps.look_for: Garrya ovata subsp. lindheimeri → accepted Garrya lindheimeri.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents one plant from appearing twice in the learner.

comparisons.title: Garryaceae vs showy-flowered asterids
comparisons.rule: Garrya is wind-pollinated and dioecious, with petal-less aments; do not expect a fused colorful corolla.

visual_lesson.caveat: Male and female Garrya plants look different when reproductive. Do not treat a lack of fruit on a staminate plant as evidence against the ID.

genera.fast_cue: opposite leathery leaves + dioecious petal-less aments + dark berry

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Current treatment recognizes Garrya lindheimeri as the accepted species; retain the older subspecies name as provenance.
Accepted; native range southwestern Texas to northeastern Mexico.
